title: Program Scheduler
description:

title: Assembler - 2nd Shift
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Solder Assembler in Oldsmar, FL for a one-year contract-to-hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Solder Assembler will assemble printed circuit boards by soldering a wide range of electronic components, inspecting for defects, and ensuring all work meets IPC quality and reliability standards. This role requires strong hands-on soldering experience, IPC-A-610 knowledge, microscope/AOI inspection ability, and comfort working 2nd shift.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Minimum 2 years of hands-on solder assembly experience in a production environment.
  • IPC-A-610 soldering experience.
  • Proficiency with IPC standards, including IPC-A-610 and IPC J-STD-001.
  • Ability to perform manual and/or selective soldering.
  • Experience soldering through-hole, SMT, BGA, QFN, CSP, and other component types.
  • Ability to solder and inspect component sizes ranging from 0201 to 1206, including BGAs and QFNs.
  • Experience with mixed-technology boards, including SMT and through-hole components.
  • Familiarity with soldering tools such as soldering irons, hot air guns, reflow ovens, and wave solder machines.
  • Strong visual inspection skills.
  • Ability to use microscopes and AOI equipment to detect solder defects.
  • Ability to identify solder defects such as bridges, cold joints, tombstoning, insufficient wetting, and voids.
  • Ability to verify solder paste, flux, and materials meet required specifications.
  • Detail-oriented approach with strong problem-solving ability.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to follow safety procedures, including hazardous material handling and PPE requirements.
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to read and write English.
  • Ability to take and pass a required medical exam.
  • Must be able to work 2nd shift; candidates will not be able to move to 1st shift.

Preferred Skills

  • Technical or vocational training in electronics assembly.
  • Knowledge of IPC-2221/2222 design standards.
  • Knowledge of lead-free and RoHS-compliant processes.
  • Familiarity with statistical process control and yield analysis.
  • Experience with PCB assembly, electronics manufacturing, solder inspection, defect identification, AOI inspection, microscope inspection, rework, selective soldering, component-level soldering, and production quality improvement.

What You’ll Do

  • Assemble printed circuit boards by soldering a wide variety of components.
  • Perform manual and/or selective soldering of through-hole, SMT, BGA, QFN, CSP, and related component types.
  • Conduct visual inspections using microscopes, AOI equipment, and other inspection tools.
  • Identify solder defects such as bridges, cold joints, tombstoning, insufficient wetting, and voids.
  • Apply IPC-A-610, IPC J-STD-001, and related IPC standards throughout the assembly process.
  • Verify solder paste, flux, and other materials meet specifications.
  • Recommend and support improvements to soldering processes, tooling, and work instructions.
  • Follow safety procedures, hazardous material handling rules, and PPE requirements.
  • Support production quality, reliability, and teamwork goals.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • Monday–Thursday.
  • 2nd shift: 3:30 PM–2:00 AM EST.
  • Candidates will not be able to move to 1st shift.
